terms.comment: From Italian schioppetto, in Latin since the Renaissance (M-O). A hunting rifle is sclopētum vēnātōrium (M-O, Egger); a pistol sclopētum minus (M-O, Busbecq). To fire a gun is sclopētāre (Traupman 324) or sclopētum displōdere (M-O s.v. shoot).

terms.gloss: a big gun, a cannon; classically a catapult
terms.comment: Classically an engine that hurls missiles, a catapult or ballista (Caes. B.G. 2.8), and the missile it throws; the Renaissance writers used it for artillery (M-O), and so does Traupman. Not for a handgun. Its other common sense is torture, or the rack.

sources: John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency, pp. 52, 187, 324, checked against the searchable text of the book (11 November 2026); p. 48.
Morgan–Owens: Adumbratio, s.v. gun, cannon, shoot.
